Normalisation is the process of making a good schema design (Principles + methodologies)
- Objective: Generate tables whose attributes depend on the complete primary key and nothing else.
- Constraint: Maintain all dependencies between attributes in a database decomposition.
Attribute dependencies are also known as functional dependencies.

Composition vs decomposition:
Top down (most common): Using scientific/mathematical solution
Bottom-up (less common): Requires some domain knowledge + intuition

- Each table schema describes one entity or relationship between entities with a PK each.
- Further split schemas (and conquer) until no anomalies are possible.
- Avoid attributes which can be often NULL.
- Link schemas via PK and FK attributes only.

- No redundancy: $math{{G-FD}^S !=F^S, \any FD \in G} (FD: functional dependency, x->A)

1NF (Atomic Attributes (no sets), “Attribute-level Normalisation”): 
Set/Multi-valued attribute should not appear
e.g. (ISBN, Title, AuthorId), (42342345356, 'Fundamentals of Databases', {3433,5522})

2NF (Strict key dependencies): require 1NF
No non-prime (not part of candidate key) attribute Y dpeends on a subset Z \sub X of a candidate key X
e.g.
NOT FULFILL: (Candidate key: {ISBN, AuthorId}, AuthorId -> AuthorName)
(ISBN, AuthorId, Author name), (423423453, 3433, Elmari), (423423453, 5522, Navathe)
-(Decompose without loss, Heath's theorem, based on AuthorId -> AuthorName)>
FULFILL:
(ISBN, AuthorId), (423423453, 3433), (423423453, 5522)
(AuthorId, Author Name), (3433, Elmari), (5522, Navathe)

3NF (Decomposition (lossless) of transitive FDs): require 2NF
All non-prime attributes Y are defined by a candidate key/prime key
NOT FULFILL: (Candidate key: {ISBN}, ISBN -> (PublisherID -> PublisherName))
(ISBN, Title, PublisherID, PublisherName), (423423453, 'Fundamentals of Databases', 3234, 'Pearson')
-(Decompose without loss (Heath's theorem) based on PublisherId -> PublisherName)->
(ISBN, Title, PublisherID), (423423453, 'Fundamentals of Databases', 3234)
(PublisherID, PublisherName), (3234, Pearson)
